title: Remove authenticator
purpose: Confirm removal of one lost sign-in factor from an account.

sections.title: Access and displayed scope
paragraphs: Requires an active account with both Staff and Superuser status. A laboratory admin role, Staff status alone or individual authenticator or email-address model permissions granted to a user or group do not open this page.
The page names the factor type and shows a summary of what will be removed: this single factor record. There is no bulk removal from the list.

items.label: Yes, I’m sure
items.description: Removes the factor. In the same step the account’s audit history records who removed it, when, and the factor’s type, enrollment and last-use times. The secret is never recorded. If the audit record cannot be written, nothing is removed.

sections.title: Effect
paragraphs: Only this factor is removed; the account, its roles and its other factors stay. Removing an authenticator app leaves any Recovery codes record in place, and removing recovery codes leaves the app. Self-service deactivation cleanup is not run. The owner can enroll a new factor from their own Two-factor authentication pages.

sections.title: Navigation
paragraphs: Home, application, model list and object breadcrumbs return to the permitted maintenance pages.
